metadata.title: Three Requirements on a Relativistic Home for MOND Phenomenology
metadata.description:
V4 adds a new section: a candidate that satisfies R1 by construction. (i) The a0-line's AQUAL free function is derived in CLOSED FORM, f(z) = (1/2)sqrt(z)sqrt(1+4z) + (1/4)asinh(2 sqrt z) - sqrt(z) with z = (g_obs/a0)^2, and its deep-MOND limit is EXACTLY (2/3) z^(3/2) — the same 3/2 power and the same 2/3 coefficient AeST's own MOND term carries, with no free constant anywhere in the chain; the phenomenological relation and the host theory's MOND term agree at leading order because of what they are, not because they were matched. (ii) The beta=1 DBI kernel is shown analytic at its minimum with every odd coefficient vanishing (exponents 2,4,6,...) and a one-half power at its wall, so it supplies 3/2 at NEITHER location. (iii) A single-argument ansatz F(Y,Q) -> F(X) with X = (Q-Q_0) - Y/2m leaves the FRW background, w = -1 and the derived a0(z) law untouched by construction, and — using the theory's own quasi-static relation Q = (1-Psi)Q_0 — has X = -Psi Q_0 - Y/2m, so the free function's argument contains the Newtonian potential directly, satisfying R1 by construction. The mass m is fixed by the deep-MOND normalisation, hence by a0, and is not a new parameter. Recorded as OPEN, not as a result: a single ANALYTIC F cannot be quadratic at the origin and |X|^(3/2) at once, and the ansatz survives only because the two regimes sit on opposite sides of X = 0; the vector sector under the ansatz, the coupling to baryons against gamma_PPN = 1, and the pressure question are all unrun.

Aether-Scalar-Tensor gravity (AeST; Skordis & Złośnik 2021, Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 161302) is the only relativistic MOND-class theory that reproduces the CMB power spectrum, and it contains a single free function F(Y,Q) that its authors leave unspecified. This paper shows that specifying it is obstructed, and extracts from the obstruction three necessary conditions on any relativistic completion of MOND phenomenology. Each condition is established by an explicit construction that satisfies the previous ones and fails the next, so the result is a filter on future theory-building rather than a single negative claim.

R1 — the free function must depend on the gradient of the TOTAL potential, not the scalar's own. With F(Y) the quasi-static reduction makes the scalar's own gradient the anomalous acceleration, and single-valuedness of F is equivalent to positivity of the longitudinal kinetic eigenvalue, which forces U(y) strictly increasing, which forces saturation U -> s, which produces a CONSTANT sunward anomaly s*a0 at every planetary distance. Perihelion precession then requires s <= 1.27e-5 (canonical footing) or 1.05e-5 (alternative), while the radial acceleration relation requires s >= 0.4348 pointwise, or 0.157-0.294 on the most generous global fit: incompatible by a factor 1.2e4 to 3.4e4. Crucially, this is specific to AeST and NOT to AQUAL, where the free function eats the total gradient and stability requires only d(g_obs)/d(g_bar) > 0 — satisfied by the exponential interpolation at minimum 0.968. The same kernel is legal in one theory and fatal in the other, purely from which gradient the free function eats. No relief exists: the external-field effect, computed for this family by two independent routes rather than imported, contributes exactly 1.000000x; a density-dependent a0 makes matters worse and is unsatisfiable below a suppression factor 0.080; solving the non-spherical problem for a Miyamoto-Nagai disc widens the requirement by 1.07-1.10x; refitting stellar mass-to-light buys 1.34x.

R2 — the cosmological background must not coincide with the deep-MOND end of the interpolation. AeST already contains the object R1 demands. An identity, verified three times independently and requiring no computer algebra, shows that AeST's aether-scalar mixing term is equivalent to an explicit +(2-K_B) a^mu a_mu piece, so the theory's apparent c_4 = 0 is an artifact of variables. Replacing F(Y,Q) by F(Z,Q) with Z = J^mu J_mu, the squared aether acceleration, then satisfies R1 exactly: J^i = grad^i Psi with unit coefficient, the quasi-static reduction becomes AQUAL exactly, the exponential kernel becomes legal, Newton's constant stays finite, and the 1 AU anomaly falls to 1e-3458.7 m/s^2 — some 3445 orders below the Sereno-Jetzer bound, replacing an anomaly that sat 1279x above it. The gap of R1 is voided. But Z-bar = 0 IDENTICALLY on FRW, so the cosmological background IS the deep-MOND end; linear cosmology sees K_B -> K_B - F_Z(0), and any F that performs the MOND interpolation has F_Z(0) = K_B exactly, so the aether's electric kinetic coefficient vanishes and the perturbation equation degenerates. F(Y) is protected only because J_Y vanishes at zero argument — the exact inverse situation.

R3 — and neither condition may be purchased with a split between the cosmological and local gravitational constants. Rescaling the free function repairs R1 and R2 simultaneously, with a non-empty window 0 < s < 0.138 at K_B = 0.25, leaving the solar-system screening untouched. The price is that the free function's normalisation becomes the sole source of Newton's constant, forcing Gtilde/G_N <= 0.121 (K_B = 0.25) or 0.048 (K_B = 0.10) against AeST's own 0.875 — an 8.3x to 20.7x split. It cannot be paid. Big-bang nucleosynthesis gives Y_p = 0.086 against an observed 0.2449 +/- 0.0040, a 42-sigma exclusion, with a closure-free backstop assuming no nucleosynthesis model at all still giving Y_p <= 0.176 at 17 sigma. The CMB result is an inconsistency rather than a tension: the gravitational sector's radiation density comes out at 0.2046 of the thermal photon density — below the gravitating density of the photons alone, whose value FIRAS fixes with no gravity anywhere in the chain — equivalent to N_eff = -3.503, missing the hard floor by 4.9x to 12.2x.

Stated against interest: gravitational waves do NOT pay this price, and the paper says so at equal volume. The tensor sector is exactly Einstein-Hilbert — on FRW plus a TT mode, J^mu = 0, Z = 0, F_munu = 0 and Y = 0 all hold identically and to all orders in the perturbation, so the dark sector carries no anisotropic stress for any free function — giving c_T = 1 and alpha_M = 0 exactly. The standard-siren amplitude's sensitivity to the rescaling is exactly zero and GW170817 places no bound. Two liabilities the same derivation creates are recorded but explicitly NOT scored, because the sharpest of them self-refutes: a tensor-only orbital-decay ledger giving an 8x deficit against B1913+16 would also exclude UNMODIFIED AeST at 77 sigma, so the ledger is incomplete rather than the theory dead.

Testable predictions. (P1) alpha_M = 0 and c_T = 1 exactly, for any free function, any rescaling, any K_B and both a0 footings — so this entire class is indistinguishable from general relativity in gravitational-wave propagation, and a confirmed alpha_M != 0 from LISA or Einstein Telescope falsifies all of it in one measurement, absorbable by no choice of free function. (P2) Any repair to the flux ledger must be period-INDEPENDENT, supplying the same fraction at every orbital period, because the decay ratio is measured at 0.16% in a 7.75 h orbit and 1.3e-4 in a 2.45 h one while a dipole enters at relative order (c/v)^2; the repair must renormalise the quadrupole coefficient itself. (P3) The F(Y) class predicts a constant sunward anomaly with a fixed planet ordering, already excluded. (P4) The F(Z) class predicts no solar-system deviation at any measurable level, ever.

Explicitly not claimed: that the three requirements are SUFFICIENT — they are necessary conditions extracted from three failures, and a completion satisfying all three is not thereby viable; that kappa = 1/2 is derived (it is FITTED, measured 0.529 +/- 0.034 from three determinations, with the distance-free one carrying an unpriced ~7% systematic); or that dark matter is absent (the full dark-matter density is retained here and the claim is "no dark-matter PARTICLE"). Whether the dark sector's dust remains bound inside galaxies is unresolved and untouched by any of this, being a Q-sector problem while all three constructions modify the Y-sector.

Unaffected, being independent of which completion carries them: the acceleration-scale normalisation a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = 9.3619e-11 m/s^2, the radial acceleration relation at 0.108 dex on 175 SPARC galaxies, weak lensing from 40 kpc to 2.2 Mpc with no dark component, the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, and a hash-frozen wide-binary prediction decided by Gaia DR4.

Every quantitative claim is reproduced by a committed, self-checking script at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula; each prints numbered checks and exits non-zero on failure. Withdrawn claims are recorded, dated, in RETRACTIONS.md — including one in this paper's own drafting, where a gravitational-wave exclusion was written from an unverified number and corrected against the committed script before filing.

The contribution is the three requirements, the identity of section 3, and the constructions that establish them — NOT the underlying theory, which is Skordis and Złośnik's.
metadata.notes: V3, settled. Architecture: three necessary conditions, each established by an explicit construction that satisfies its predecessors and fails it. R1 = the free function must eat the TOTAL gradient (else saturation, and a 1.2e4-3.4e4 ephemeris/RAR gap). R2 = eating the total gradient must not destabilise the vector sector (the Z-form's ghost, C_V = -1.50, fatal over the solar system and the optical galaxy). R3 = the repair may not be bought with a Gtilde/G_N split (BBN -42 sigma; gravitational radiation below the photon density). R2 is the sharpest as a DESIGN constraint because it is not about any particular invariant: whatever the free function eats, the same limit that produces Newtonian screening must not be the limit that destabilises another sector. Stated against interest: gravitational waves do NOT pay R3's price, and one liability is unscored because the identical ledger would exclude the unmodified parent theory. kappa = 1/2 is FITTED, never derived. Underlying theory: Skordis and Zlosnik, PRL 127, 161302.
